title: Company overview
text:
# Company overview

> Fictional demonstration content. Not a real vendor claim.

VANTER Engineering Systems is a fictional enterprise-software provider headquartered in Rotterdam, Netherlands. The company develops software for industrial engineering, capital-project execution, asset information and system integration. This knowledge base is a synthetic demonstration, not evidence about a real company.

VANTER serves engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contractors; industrial asset owners; engineering consultancies; and construction programme teams. Example sectors are energy, chemicals, advanced manufacturing and infrastructure. VANTER does not provide physical construction services or engineering sign-off.

Its product family consists of DesignHub (engineering information), ProjectFlow (project execution), AssetTwin (asset context), and Connect (integrations). These are separate modules that can be licensed independently. Integration and deployment requirements differ by module.

The company's illustrative proposition is “Engineering complexity. Made manageable.” Its software is intended to improve traceability, coordination and information access; the company makes no universal claim of quantified cost or schedule savings. A discovery workshop is required to evaluate fit for any specific project.

title: Industries and audiences
text:
# Industries and audiences

> Fictional demonstration content. Not a real vendor claim.

VANTER targets complex, multi-stakeholder industrial programmes. In chemicals and process industries, common challenges include equipment-tag consistency, controlled revisions and handover records. In energy, teams may need cross-contractor information coordination. In advanced manufacturing, frequent design changes and commissioning dependencies can complicate execution. In infrastructure, geographically distributed suppliers and phased delivery create coordination challenges.

Typical users include project engineers, design managers, project controls teams, construction managers, asset-information managers, IT architects, procurement teams and executives. Job title alone does not establish user intent. Ask what outcome the visitor wants before assuming which product is appropriate.

Engineers generally need supported formats, revision logic, permissions and examples. IT teams need deployment, APIs, identity and security. Procurement teams need licensing scope, support, implementation dependencies and vendor evaluation. Executives need strategic fit, implementation risk and a credible evaluation approach. These are guidance patterns, not rigid personas.

VANTER's fictional geographic focus is Benelux, Germany, the UK and the Nordic countries. No actual regional office, client deployment or certification is implied.

title: DesignHub product specification
text:
# DesignHub product specification

> Fictional demonstration content. Not a real vendor claim.

DesignHub is a controlled workspace for engineering documents, equipment registers, drawing metadata and revision history. Its core objects are project, discipline, document, revision, equipment tag and change request. Teams can link a drawing revision to an equipment tag and record its review status.

Supported demonstration imports: PDF documents; CSV equipment registers; IFC 4 model metadata; and exported drawing registers in CSV. DesignHub does not natively author CAD geometry or edit IFC models. Native proprietary CAD formats require an external converter or integration assessment.

Capabilities: document versioning; approval workflows with configurable reviewers; metadata search; equipment-tag linking; audit events; role-based permissions; and exportable handover registers. Revision states are Draft, In Review, Approved and Superseded. Approved records are not silently overwritten; a new revision is created.

Integration: Connect can synchronize selected metadata with other systems. No real-time bidirectional synchronization is guaranteed. DesignHub may be used without ProjectFlow, but change-request linkage is richer when both are deployed.

Limitations: not a full common data environment certification claim; not a 3D model authoring tool; not a substitute for engineering quality assurance. Performance for very large models must be tested in a pilot.

title: ProjectFlow product specification
text:
# ProjectFlow product specification

> Fictional demonstration content. Not a real vendor claim.

ProjectFlow coordinates work packages, project milestones, contractor responsibilities, issues and change requests on industrial capital projects. A work package may have an owner, due date, dependencies, status and links to engineering records.

Core functions: configurable project dashboards; issue tracking; milestone dependencies; change-request registers; action ownership; document links; and controlled status reports. Supported import for baseline schedules is CSV; direct native scheduling-system integrations are not included by default.

The change process records an initiating issue, affected packages, assigned reviewers, decision, target date and closure evidence. If DesignHub is deployed, a change can reference an engineering document revision. ProjectFlow does not automatically determine the commercial cost of a change or certify its technical validity.

ProjectFlow can be used by EPC contractors and owners, with separate project-level permissions. It is not a replacement for a full enterprise resource planning platform, a contract management system or a scheduling engine. It provides coordination and traceability, not automated construction execution.

A pilot should validate the organization's work-package taxonomy, status conventions, reporting cadence and contractor-access model.

title: AssetTwin product specification
text:
# AssetTwin product specification

> Fictional demonstration content. Not a real vendor claim.

AssetTwin brings together equipment-tag records, maintenance context, documents and selected operating-data references for an industrial asset. It is a digital asset-information workspace, not a physics simulation or a live operational control system.

Capabilities: asset hierarchy; tag-to-document links; equipment attributes; maintenance-event references; searchable handover records; and a contextual view of data received from approved integrations. Data ingestion can use structured CSV and configured Connect connectors. Near-real-time refresh may be possible for supported feeds, but is not assumed in the baseline demonstration.

AssetTwin can consume a validated handover register from DesignHub. It does not guarantee that upstream information is complete or correct. It does not send control commands to plant equipment, perform predictive maintenance autonomously or replace safety-critical systems.

Use cases include finding the latest approved pump datasheet, locating commissioning records and seeing which asset records are missing required fields. The quality of output depends on the completeness of asset identifiers and source-system governance.

A pilot should check tag naming, asset hierarchy, permissions, source-system ownership and data-refresh expectations.

title: Connect integration specification
text:
# Connect integration specification

> Fictional demonstration content. Not a real vendor claim.

Connect is VANTER's integration layer for exchanging selected metadata and structured records between VANTER modules and approved external systems. It supports REST/JSON APIs, CSV batch imports and exports, webhook events for configured workflows, and scheduled synchronization jobs.

Example data objects include document metadata, equipment tags, work-package identifiers, change-request statuses and asset records. Every connector needs an explicit mapping specification, authentication configuration and error-handling policy.

Baseline demonstration behavior: a scheduled sync every 60 minutes is available for CSV-based exchanges; API-triggered updates depend on the integration design. Connect does not imply universal plug-and-play compatibility with SAP, Primavera, Autodesk, AVEVA or any other named vendor. Any such integration requires a feasibility review and potentially a custom adapter.

Connect logs synchronization attempts, rejects invalid mappings and can flag duplicates for review. It cannot resolve contradictory source data automatically without defined precedence rules. It is not an industrial control gateway and must not be used for safety-critical commands.

title: Reference architecture
text:
# Reference architecture

> Fictional demonstration content. Not a real vendor claim.

The illustrative VANTER architecture has four layers: user interface, application services, structured document and record storage, and Connect integrations. DesignHub, ProjectFlow and AssetTwin share identity and tenant context but maintain product-specific records. An organization may deploy one or more modules.

The demonstration assumes a browser interface, a backend API, object storage for files, a relational database for structured records, and a search index for approved content. These are architectural concepts, not claims about a production implementation.

A knowledge-aware AI assistant should use retrieval from explicitly approved documents, record source IDs, and distinguish sourced facts from general explanatory text. It must not be granted direct write access to engineering approval states. Generated pages should be represented as structured blocks with source references, rather than arbitrary unreviewed HTML.

Suggested generated-page block types: executive summary, relevant products, technical fit, implementation considerations, source documents, clarifying question and next step. A renderer validates block schemas and refuses unsupported product claims. Every product-specific statement should be traceable to a knowledge-base document.

Availability, scale and resilience targets are to be defined during discovery; no uptime SLA is specified in this demo.

title: Integration and data formats
text:
# Integration and data formats

> Fictional demonstration content. Not a real vendor claim.

DesignHub accepts PDF, CSV registers and IFC 4 metadata imports. ProjectFlow accepts CSV schedule baselines and work-package registers. AssetTwin accepts structured asset registers in CSV. Connect exposes REST/JSON endpoints, configured webhooks and scheduled CSV exchange.

Illustrative integration process: identify system of record; define entity mapping; choose one-way or two-way transfer; set refresh frequency; agree error handling; validate a sample dataset; then conduct user acceptance testing. The initial pilot should prioritize one or two integrations, not attempt enterprise-wide connectivity.

For IFC, the demo supports metadata extraction and links to model references, not native geometric editing. For CAD authoring systems, an export or converter is required. For ERP or maintenance-management systems, compatibility is unconfirmed until an interface review.

Important constraints: source data quality remains the customer's responsibility; identity and authorization must be mapped; duplicate tags may require human resolution; historical revisions should not be overwritten by a sync; integration latency depends on the configured workflow.

Do not describe any third-party vendor integration as certified, supported out of the box or commercially available without separate evidence.

title: Security and governance
text:
# Security and governance

> Fictional demonstration content. Not a real vendor claim.

VANTER's fictional baseline design supports role-based access control, organization/project separation, audit logging and configurable document visibility. Proposed enterprise authentication is SAML 2.0 or OpenID Connect, subject to implementation scope. Encryption in transit and at rest is an architectural requirement for the prototype design, not a verified production certification.

Roles may include Organization Admin, Project Admin, Contributor, Reviewer and Viewer. Access to generated AI content must be filtered using the same document permissions as ordinary search. An AI response must never expose a restricted source merely because a visitor asks for it.

The demo has no ISO 27001, SOC 2, GDPR compliance certification or penetration-test report. Do not claim any certification or legal compliance status. Data residency, retention, subprocessors, incident response, and contractual security terms require vendor due diligence before procurement.

AI-specific safeguards: retrieve only authorized material; show citations; do not infer confidential facts; flag uncertain statements; do not allow an agent to approve engineering changes, make procurement commitments or issue safety-critical instructions. External technical knowledge must be clearly labeled as general reference information rather than company policy.

title: Deployment and technical prerequisites
text:
# Deployment and technical prerequisites

> Fictional demonstration content. Not a real vendor claim.

The baseline concept is a vendor-managed cloud application with separate organization workspaces. Private-cloud or on-premises deployment is not included as a standard demo capability; requests require an architectural and commercial assessment.

A pilot needs an executive sponsor, product owner, IT/security contact, representative users, sample documents, agreed access roles and a clear use case. Browser access and enterprise identity integration should be tested early. For external contractor collaboration, project-specific invitations and access expiration need to be defined.

Illustrative onboarding stages: discovery; data sampling; configuration; integration proof of concept; user acceptance; phased rollout. The customer must supply approved source material and identify a system of record for each data class.

No hard claims are made for maximum file size, concurrent users, latency, uptime, geographic hosting location or disaster-recovery objectives. These values are deliberately unspecified and must not be invented by the AI agent.

Success criteria should be agreed before implementation: e.g., time to locate a revision, completeness of handover records, or turnaround time for a change request.

title: EPC contractor solution
text:
# EPC contractor solution

> Fictional demonstration content. Not a real vendor claim.

EPC contractors must coordinate design packages, subcontractors, changes and construction progress across disciplines. VANTER's proposed combination is DesignHub for engineering records, ProjectFlow for work packages and change coordination, and Connect for exchanging approved metadata.

Illustrative journey: a design manager publishes a revised drawing in DesignHub; the project engineer links it to a change request; ProjectFlow identifies affected work packages; designated reviewers assess impacts; the team closes the issue with a documented decision. This is an illustrative workflow, not an automated guarantee of impact detection.

Typical evaluation questions: How are revisions approved? Which parties need external access? What is the source of the schedule baseline? How are contractor identifiers mapped? Which reports are required for the client?

Do not promise automatic prevention of delays or elimination of rework. A pilot should test a specific work-package and revision-control scenario with representative documents.

title: Owner-operator solution
text:
# Owner-operator solution

> Fictional demonstration content. Not a real vendor claim.

Industrial owner-operators need reliable information from project handover into operations. The proposed VANTER journey combines DesignHub for approved engineering records, AssetTwin for asset-centric context and Connect for transferring validated equipment data.

Example: an asset-information manager receives a handover register; checks tag completeness; links approved datasheets and commissioning evidence; then makes the resulting records searchable by maintenance teams. AssetTwin helps locate information but does not validate engineering correctness automatically.

Evaluation questions: Which tag naming convention is authoritative? What information is mandatory at handover? Who owns maintenance data? How will obsolete revisions be handled? What records may contractors access after commissioning?

No claim is made that AssetTwin replaces an enterprise asset management system or can predict failures without additional, validated capabilities.

title: Engineering consultancy solution
text:
# Engineering consultancy solution

> Fictional demonstration content. Not a real vendor claim.

Engineering consultancies often need cross-discipline document control, controlled reviews and transparent handover to clients. DesignHub is the primary VANTER module for this audience; Connect may support exports to client systems.

An illustrative workflow includes creating a document register, assigning review owners, tracking approval states and producing a controlled handover package. Where the consultancy also manages site coordination, ProjectFlow may be relevant.

Evaluation questions: Which document numbering rules are used? What review gates are mandatory? Do clients require IFC metadata or only approved PDFs? What is the expected volume of external reviewers? Is a client-specific export format needed?

DesignHub does not author engineering calculations or replace discipline-specific CAD tools. A consultancy should validate compatibility with its actual toolchain before procurement.

title: Licensing and procurement
text:
# Licensing and procurement

> Fictional demonstration content. Not a real vendor claim.

VANTER products are licensed as separate enterprise modules: DesignHub, ProjectFlow, AssetTwin and Connect. The fictional commercial model is an annual subscription with scope based on enabled modules, named internal users, external collaborators, project count and integration complexity.

No public list prices, discounts, minimum commitments or standardized per-seat rates are defined in this demonstration. The AI agent must not quote a price or invent a commercial offer. Procurement should request a scoped proposal.

A vendor evaluation should cover required functions, data ownership, export options, integration feasibility, security review, implementation responsibilities, support coverage and contract exit arrangements. External collaborators may require additional licensing; this is not settled in the demo.

Recommended next step: document number of users, sites/projects, required modules, integrations, data volume and expected timeline, then request a tailored commercial discussion. A request for proposal can reference the product specifications and technical prerequisites in this knowledge base.

title: Implementation approach
text:
# Implementation approach

> Fictional demonstration content. Not a real vendor claim.

VANTER recommends a phased implementation rather than immediate enterprise-wide deployment. Phase 1: discovery and use-case definition. Phase 2: source-data review and governance. Phase 3: limited configuration and one or two integrations. Phase 4: pilot with representative users. Phase 5: evaluate outcomes and decide whether to expand.

Illustrative pilot duration is 6–10 weeks after prerequisites are available. This is a planning assumption for the fictional prototype, not a binding delivery promise. Complex data cleanup or integration dependencies may extend the timeline.

Responsibilities: the customer provides approved data, business owners, security requirements and acceptance criteria; the implementation team configures the selected modules, maps agreed interfaces and documents limitations. The customer retains responsibility for engineering approvals and data accuracy.

Pilot deliverables may include configured workflows, mapped sample records, user training, issue log, acceptance test results and a go/no-go recommendation. Avoid claims that deployment is instant or requires no IT involvement.

title: Business case and evaluation
text:
# Business case and evaluation

> Fictional demonstration content. Not a real vendor claim.

The business case should begin with measurable workflow problems rather than an assumed return on investment. Examples: time spent locating approved revisions; hours required to compile handover registers; overdue change requests; and duplicated data entry across systems.

Suggested evaluation method: establish baseline with a small user group; run the same tasks with the pilot; record task completion time, accuracy, user confidence and unresolved issues; account for implementation and subscription costs; then assess whether expansion is justified.

Illustrative calculation only: annual net benefit = verified annual time savings valued at an agreed labor rate + other validated benefits − annual recurring costs − annualized implementation costs. No default percentage savings, payback period or ROI is asserted.

Executives should see strategic fit, risks, dependencies, governance and next-step decisions. The AI agent may build a qualitative business-case outline but must not fabricate customer results or benchmark statistics.

title: Frequently asked questions
text:
# Frequently asked questions

> Fictional demonstration content. Not a real vendor claim.

Q: Can we buy DesignHub without ProjectFlow? A: Yes, modules can be licensed separately.

Q: Does DesignHub edit CAD models? A: No. It manages documents, metadata and revisions; native authoring remains in external tools.

Q: Does VANTER support IFC? A: The demonstration specifies IFC 4 metadata import in DesignHub, not geometry editing.

Q: Can ProjectFlow replace Primavera or an ERP? A: No. It coordinates packages and changes; native third-party integration is not assumed.

Q: Does AssetTwin control plant equipment? A: No. It is an information workspace, not an operational control system.

Q: Is SAP integration certified? A: No such certification is claimed. A feasibility assessment is required.

Q: Can we deploy on premises? A: Not as a baseline capability. This requires assessment.

Q: How much does it cost? A: There is no published price in this demonstration; scope a proposal.

Q: Is VANTER ISO 27001 certified? A: No certification is asserted in this fictional prototype.

Q: How quickly can we pilot? A: An illustrative planning range is 6–10 weeks after prerequisites are met.

Q: Can the AI approve engineering changes? A: No. Human reviewers retain authority.

title: Support, escalation and AI response policy
text:
# Support, escalation and AI response policy

> Fictional demonstration content. Not a real vendor claim.

For this fictional prototype, standard support channels are an in-app support request and a customer success contact assigned during onboarding. No phone number, email address, office address beyond Rotterdam, or support portal URL is defined. The AI must not invent them.

Incident categories: access issue; data import problem; integration error; product defect; enhancement request; and security concern. Severity definitions, response-time targets and support hours are not specified and require a service agreement.

Escalate to a human when a visitor requests pricing, contractual commitments, security attestations, unsupported integrations, safety-critical recommendations, or information that is missing or contradictory. Ask for the minimum information needed to route the request; do not request confidential project documents in an anonymous public session.

AI behavior: identify the visitor's objective; retrieve relevant approved sources; offer a concise answer and evidence links; ask a clarifying question only if it changes the recommended solution; generate a structured personal workspace; separate company facts from general background; state uncertainty clearly; never fabricate case studies, clients, integrations, certifications, pricing, SLAs or performance metrics.

The public prototype should use only synthetic documents. No personal visitor data should be retained by default. A production implementation requires privacy, security and consent review.

title: Industrial project lifecycle and information needs
text:
# Industrial project lifecycle and information needs

An industrial capital project can progress through investment decision, feasibility and concept, permitting and design development, detailed design, procurement and construction, commissioning, and operation. The exact stages and responsibilities depend on the contract and jurisdiction. The SEVERIN reference presentation maps responsibilities across these phases; VANTER uses this as **domain inspiration**, not a claim about SEVERIN software.

At feasibility stage, owners need scope definition, budget assumptions, risks and schedule alternatives. During design, engineering teams need controlled revisions, discipline coordination and issue tracking. During construction, managers need package status, decisions, site issues and evidence. At handover, owners need reliable as-built documents, equipment registers and operating records.

VANTER mapping (fictional): DesignHub manages document/revision metadata; ProjectFlow manages work packages and decisions; Connect handles assessed data exchanges; AssetTwin organises selected handover asset records. No VANTER module independently supplies legal approvals, engineering sign-off, or a complete project-delivery service.

Source boundary: the lifecycle and service categories are grounded in SEVERIN DEVELOPMENT's presentation. Product mapping is newly invented for the VANTER demo.

title: EPC, EPCM and stakeholder responsibilities
text:
# EPC, EPCM and stakeholder responsibilities

EPC stands for Engineering, Procurement and Construction; EPCM stands for Engineering, Procurement and Construction Management. The SEVERIN presentation distinguishes a general construction contracting component within EPC from procurement/tender and construction-management functions within EPCM. The exact allocation of liability and procurement contracts must always be verified against project contracts.

Typical stakeholders and information needs:
- Asset owner / investor: programme exposure, investment assumptions, decision visibility, commissioning and handover readiness.
- Project director: schedule dependencies, package status, scope changes and accountability.
- Design manager / engineer: document revisions, IFC metadata, technical review decisions and interfaces.
- Construction manager: site issues, contractor coordination, approvals and close-out evidence.
- Procurement / commercial: supplier scope, licensing, implementation effort, support and auditability.
- IT / security: identity, deployment options, integrations, data ownership and security limitations.

An AI guide should ask about the **task**, not infer it from title alone. If asked for contractual responsibility, it should explain that the answer depends on the agreement and direct users to legal/project specialists.

title: Industrial project scenarios for adaptive pages
text:
# Industrial project scenarios for adaptive pages

These are fictional situations inspired by the diversity of industrial facilities in the reference portfolio. They are **not** VANTER customer projects and must never be presented as customer testimonials.

## Brownfield production-plant upgrade
An engineering manager needs to track revised drawings while a production facility remains operational. Recommend DesignHub for controlled revisions and ProjectFlow for review actions. Ask about existing document formats, contractor count and approval process. Do not claim production downtime reduction.

## New industrial processing facility
A project director wants visibility across concept, detailed design, contractor work packages and commissioning. Recommend ProjectFlow plus DesignHub; explain handover as a separate AssetTwin assessment. Ask about project phase and reporting systems.

## Industrial park with multiple tenants
An owner needs information boundaries between tenant projects, infrastructure packages and operators. Discuss project-level access and integration discovery. Do not promise tenant data isolation certification without evidence.

## Plant asset handover
An operations lead wants an equipment-tag register connected to as-built records. Discuss DesignHub export, AssetTwin records and quality checks. Do not promise a complete digital twin from arbitrary drawings.

Reference examples include a starch plant reconstruction and industrial park master planning. Their real customer names, locations and metrics are excluded from the public VANTER demo.

title: Evidence boundaries and safe AI generation
text:
# Evidence boundaries and safe AI generation

Knowledge classes:
1. **VANTER fictional specifications** (VNT-01–VNT-18): authoritative only within this demonstration universe.
2. **Adapted industrial domain context** (VNT-19–VNT-21): grounded in SEVERIN reference material, but not evidence of VANTER deployment or performance.
3. **External general explanation**: allowed only when clearly labelled as general guidance, not a VANTER feature or legal/technical assurance.
4. **Private contract register**: not indexed, not shown, not summarised in the public prototype.

Generation rules: cite document IDs on every substantive claim; never invent clients, project outcomes, prices, certifications, security attestations, native integrations or product performance. Where source evidence is missing, say so and offer a discovery step. Never reproduce the real company's branding, customer list, project photos or contractual information as VANTER proof.

The source presentation reflects its publication period. Do not assume 'ongoing' projects or certification statements remain current in 2026.
